nodes.description: Expanded polyglutamine ataxin-1, ataxin-2, and TBP adopt aberrant conformations and form nuclear and cytoplasmic inclusions. Sequestration of chaperones, ubiquitin-proteasome and autophagy components, and interacting partners progressively impairs neuronal proteostasis, contributing to Purkinje-cell and brainstem-neuron dysfunction. This proteostatic stress is a convergent downstream consequence of the polyglutamine subtypes and is described mechanistically here without an independent ADCA-I-specific quantitative claim.

nodes.description: ADCA-I is unified by a dominant ataxia-plus phenotype, not by one proximal lesion. Coding polyglutamine expansions, other coding or noncoding repeat expansions, and conventional sequence or copy-number variants initiate distinct molecular cascades that converge on cerebellar and variably extracerebellar neurodegeneration.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia type I: a review of the phenotypic and genotypic characteristics.
evidence.snippet: Type I ADCA can be further divided based on the proposed pathogenetic mechanism into 3 subclasses: subclass 1 includes type I ADCA caused by CAG repeat expansions such as SCA1-SCA3, SCA17, and DRPLA, subclass 2 includes trinucleotide repeat expansions that fall outside of the protein-coding regions of the disease gene including SCA8, SCA10 and SCA12. Subclass 3 contains disorders caused by specific gene deletions, missense mutation, and nonsense mutation and includes SCA13, SCA14, SCA15/16, SCA27 and SCA28.
